title: MATH GAOKAO - 266
description: Authentic-style mathematics problems inspired by China’s Gaokao — build deeper understanding, sharper thinking, and real exam readiness.

questions.concept: Left-Hand Limit of a Piecewise Function
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a left-hand limit by selecting the appropriate piece of a piecewise function.
questions.question: Let \(f(x)=\begin{cases}x^2+1,&x<2,\\3x-4,&x\ge2.\end{cases}\) Find \(\lim_{x\to2^-} f(x)\).
questions.explanation: For \(x\to2^-\), we have \(x<2\), so use \(f(x)=x^2+1\). Substituting \(x=2\) gives \(2^2+1=5\). Therefore, \(\lim_{x\to2^-} f(x)=5\).
questions.hint: Since \(x\) approaches \(2\) from the left, use the formula for \(x<2\).

questions.concept: Right-Hand Limit of a Piecewise Function
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a right-hand limit by selecting the appropriate piece of a piecewise function.
questions.question: Let \(f(x)=\begin{cases}2x+1,&x<1,\\x^2+3,&x\ge1.\end{cases}\) Find \(\lim_{x\to1^+} f(x)\).
questions.explanation: For \(x\to1^+\), we have \(x>1\), so use \(f(x)=x^2+3\). Substituting \(x=1\) gives \(1^2+3=4\). Thus \(\lim_{x\to1^+} f(x)=4\).
questions.hint: Since \(x\) approaches \(1\) from the right, use the formula for \(x\ge1\).

questions.concept: One-Sided Limit of an Absolute Value Quotient
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a left-hand limit involving absolute value by simplifying according to the sign of \(x\).
questions.question: Find \(\lim_{x\to0^-}\frac{|x|}{x}\).
questions.explanation: For \(x<0\), \(|x|=-x\), so \(\frac{|x|}{x}=\frac{-x}{x}=-1\) for \(x\neq0\). Therefore, as \(x\to0^-\), the quotient is constantly \(-1\), so the limit is \(-1\).
questions.hint: Determine the expression for \(|x|\) when \(x\) is negative.

questions.concept: One-Sided Limit of a Rational Function with a Removable Discontinuity
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a right-hand limit by factoring and simplifying a rational expression.
questions.question: Find \(\lim_{x\to2^+}\frac{x^2-4}{x-2}\).
questions.explanation: Factor the numerator: \(x^2-4=(x-2)(x+2)\). For \(x\neq2\), \(\frac{x^2-4}{x-2}=x+2\). As \(x\to2^+\), \(x+2\to4\). Hence the limit is \(4\).

questions.learningObjective: Determine the sign of an infinite one-sided limit from the denominator.
questions.question: Find \(\lim_{x\to1^-}\frac{1}{x-1}\) in the extended sense.
questions.explanation: As \(x\to1^-\), we have \(x<1\), so \(x-1\) is negative and tends to \(0\). Therefore \(\frac{1}{x-1}\) decreases without bound, so \(\lim_{x\to1^-}\frac{1}{x-1}=-\infty\).
questions.hint: Check whether \(x-1\) is positive or negative when \(x\) is slightly less than \(1\).

questions.concept: Right-Hand Limit at a Domain Endpoint
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a right-hand limit of a square-root function at its domain endpoint.
questions.question: Find \(\lim_{x\to0^+}\sqrt{x}\).
questions.explanation: For \(x>0\), \(\sqrt{x}\) is defined. As \(x\to0^+\) through positive values, \(\sqrt{x}\to0\). Thus the right-hand limit is \(0\).
questions.hint: Consider the values of \(\sqrt{x}\) for small positive \(x\).

questions.concept: Existence of a Two-Sided Limit from One-Sided Limits
questions.learningObjective: Determine a two-sided limit by comparing left-hand and right-hand limits.
questions.question: Let \(f(x)=\begin{cases}x+1,&x<2,\\2x-1,&x\ge2.\end{cases}\) Find \(\lim_{x\to2} f(x)\).
questions.explanation: For \(x\to2^-\), use \(x+1\), so the left-hand limit is \(2+1=3\). For \(x\to2^+\), use \(2x-1\), so the right-hand limit is \(2(2)-1=3\). Since both one-sided limits equal \(3\), the two-sided limit is \(3\).
questions.hint: Compute the left-hand and right-hand limits separately and compare them.

questions.concept: Parameter Condition for Equal One-Sided Limits
questions.learningObjective: Find a parameter value that makes the left-hand and right-hand limits equal.
questions.question: Let \(f(x)=\begin{cases}x^2+a,&x<1,\\2x+1,&x>1.\end{cases}\) If \(\lim_{x\to1^-} f(x)=\lim_{x\to1^+} f(x)\), find \(a\).
questions.explanation: As \(x\to1^-\), \(f(x)=x^2+a\), so the left-hand limit is \(1^2+a=1+a\). As \(x\to1^+\), \(f(x)=2x+1\), so the right-hand limit is \(2(1)+1=3\). Equating gives \(1+a=3\), hence \(a=2\).
questions.hint: Evaluate each one-sided limit in terms of \(a\) and set them equal.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a right-hand limit involving a square root by multiplying by the conjugate.
questions.question: Find \(\lim_{x\to0^+}\frac{\sqrt{x+1}-1}{x}\).
questions.hint: Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate of the numerator.

questions.learningObjective: Use given one-sided limits of a piecewise function to solve for two parameters and compute their sum.
questions.question: Let \(f(x)=\begin{cases}x^2+a,&x<2,\\bx+1,&x>2.\end{cases}\) If \(\lim_{x\to2^-} f(x)=5\) and \(\lim_{x\to2^+} f(x)=7\), find \(a+b\).
questions.hint: Substitute the limiting value of \(x\) into each piece and set equal to the given one-sided limits.
